title: The Music Between the Notes
title_ja: 音と音の間にある音楽
fact_notes: 人物、具体的な出来事・実験・記録は架空の教材例。実在の調査や統計の結果ではない。参考リンクは制作台帳であり外部の実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: A group of young musicians was rehearsing a short piece for a performance at a community hall.
sentences.ja: 若い音楽家のグループが地域のホールでの発表に向け、短い曲を練習していた。

sentences.en: They had practiced their individual parts carefully and could play almost every note without making mistakes.
sentences.ja: 各自のパートを丁寧に練習しており、ほとんどすべての音を間違えずに演奏できた。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, when the group played together, the music seemed hurried and difficult to follow.
sentences.ja: それでも合奏すると音楽がせわしなく、流れを追いにくく感じられた。

sentences.en: The conductor asked the musicians to listen to a recording of their rehearsal before trying again.
sentences.ja: 指揮者は再び演奏する前に練習の録音を聴くよう求めた。

sentences.en: As they listened, several students noticed that the quiet moments between musical phrases had almost disappeared.
sentences.ja: 聴いていると、数人の生徒が音楽のフレーズ間の静かな瞬間がほとんど消えていることに気づいた。

sentences.en: Each musician had been eager to begin the next phrase at exactly the right moment.
sentences.ja: 各音楽家は次のフレーズを正確な瞬間に始めようと熱心だった。

sentences.en: However, their attention to individual timing had made it difficult to notice how the whole piece was developing.
sentences.ja: しかし個々のタイミングへの意識によって曲全体の展開に気づくことが難しくなっていた。

sentences.en: The conductor suggested that they practice listening as carefully as they practiced producing sound.
sentences.ja: 指揮者は音を出す練習と同じくらい丁寧に聴く練習をするよう提案した。

sentences.en: During the next rehearsal, the musicians marked several places where they would breathe and wait together.
sentences.ja: 次の練習では、一緒に息を吸って待つ場所をいくつか印した。

sentences.en: They discussed the character of each phrase and the way it was connected to the phrase that followed.
sentences.ja: 各フレーズの特徴と次のフレーズとのつながりを話し合った。

sentences.en: Instead of concentrating only on the accuracy of their own notes, they began to pay attention to the sound around them.
sentences.ja: 自分の音の正確さだけに集中せず、周囲の音に注意を向け始めた。

sentences.en: The group recorded another performance and compared it with the earlier version.
sentences.ja: 再び演奏を録音し、以前のものと比較した。

sentences.en: The musicians felt that the new version had a clearer shape, although the actual notes had not changed.
sentences.ja: 実際の音は変わっていないが、新しい演奏にはより明確な構成があると感じた。

sentences.en: They invited two friends to listen to both recordings without telling them which was the newer one.
sentences.ja: どちらが新しいか伝えず、友人二人に両方の録音を聴いてもらった。

sentences.en: The friends described different impressions, but both noticed the contrast in the way the phrases were connected.
sentences.ja: 友人たちは異なる印象を述べたが、フレーズのつながり方の違いには二人とも気づいた。

sentences.en: The musicians treated these comments as useful feedback rather than as a final judgment of their work.
sentences.ja: 音楽家たちは意見を作品の最終評価ではなく有用なフィードバックとして受け止めた。

sentences.en: By the day of the performance, the group had learned to value the spaces between sounds.
sentences.ja: 発表当日までに、グループは音と音の間を大切にすることを学んだ。

sentences.en: Silence was no longer simply a moment when nobody was playing.
sentences.ja: 沈黙はもはや単に誰も演奏していない瞬間ではなかった。

sentences.en: It could help create expectation, separate ideas, and give a listener time to understand a musical phrase.
sentences.ja: それは期待を生み、考えを区切り、聴き手にフレーズを理解する時間を与え得た。

sentences.en: For these musicians, learning to perform together meant learning to share both sound and silence.
sentences.ja: 音楽家たちにとって合奏を学ぶことは、音と沈黙の両方を共有することだった。

questions.prompt: What had the musicians practiced before playing together?
options: The design of the community hall.
questions.explanation_ja: 各自のパートを練習した。

questions.prompt: What problem appeared during the group rehearsal?
options: The music seemed hurried and hard to follow.
The hall was too small to enter.
questions.explanation_ja: せわしなく流れが追いにくかった。

questions.prompt: What did students notice in their first recording?
options: Quiet moments between phrases had nearly disappeared.
Several extra instruments had been added.
The conductor had changed the piece completely.
The listeners had made too much noise.
questions.explanation_ja: フレーズ間の静かな瞬間がほぼなくなった。

questions.prompt: Why did playing notes accurately fail to solve the problem?
options: The piece contained no musical phrases.
The players paid too little attention to the whole piece.
The students had never practiced individually.
questions.explanation_ja: 個人のタイミングに注意しすぎ、全体を聴けなかった。

questions.prompt: What did the musicians mark in their music?
options: Places to breathe and wait together.
questions.explanation_ja: 一緒に息を吸い待つ場所。

questions.prompt: What did they do after changing their approach?
options: They wrote a completely different piece.
They stopped listening to each other.
They recorded and compared another performance.
questions.explanation_ja: 新しい録音を以前の録音と比較した。

questions.prompt: How did they present the recordings to their friends?
options: With a demand for identical opinions.
Without saying which one was newer.
After declaring which one was better.
By playing only the later version.
questions.explanation_ja: 新旧を知らせずに聴いてもらった。
作品に関する有用な反応・意見。

questions.prompt: Why was silence valuable to the group?
options: It allowed the musicians to avoid all practice.
It guaranteed that all listeners would agree.
It removed the need to play correct notes.
It could shape the music and help listeners follow phrases.
questions.explanation_ja: 曲の構成を作り、聴き手の理解を助ける。

options: Playing together involves sharing timing, listening, and silence.
A good performer never listens to others.
Every musical phrase should be played without a pause.
Individual accuracy is the only goal of performance.
questions.explanation_ja: 合奏は音を出すだけでなく聴くことと沈黙の共有。

grammar.explanation_ja: without＋動名詞は〜することなく。

grammar.focus: had made it difficult to notice
grammar.explanation_ja: make it＋形容詞＋to不定詞は〜を難しくする。
関係代名詞thatがphraseを修飾する。

grammar.focus: although the actual notes had not changed

discourse.role_ja: 個人練習の成果と合奏の課題を対比。
個人の意識と全体への注意の違いを示す。
個人の正確さだけを重視する方法からの転換。
同じ音であっても印象が変わったことを示す。

paraphrases.source: They had practiced their individual parts carefully and could play almost every note without making mistakes.
paraphrases.rewrite: They had worked carefully on their separate parts and could perform nearly all the notes correctly.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: ほぼすべての音を正しく演奏できた。

paraphrases.source: However, their attention to individual timing had made it difficult to notice how the whole piece was developing.
paraphrases.rewrite: Focusing on their own timing had prevented them from fully noticing the development of the music as a whole.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 自分のタイミングへの集中が全体の理解を妨げた。

paraphrases.source: They discussed the character of each phrase and the way it was connected to the phrase that followed.
paraphrases.rewrite: They talked about the nature of each musical idea and its relationship to the next one.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: フレーズの特徴と次とのつながりを議論した。

paraphrases.source: The musicians felt that the new version had a clearer shape, although the actual notes had not changed.
paraphrases.rewrite: The group believed the later recording had a more distinct overall form even though it contained the same notes.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 音は同じでも全体の形が明瞭になった。

cloze.explanation_ja: 静かな瞬間がなくなった。
沈黙は期待を生むことがある。
